title: The week the Sun turned blue 🔵
subject: smoke
description:
Would you have thought it was the end of the world? 👇

In September 1950, smoke from Canada's Chinchaga fire darkened Ontario at midday and turned the Sun and Moon blue as far away as Europe. It is still the largest fire on record in North America.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Chinchaga fire" (citing Field 2008 and the Edmonton Journal); University of Alberta Folio, "The year the sun and moon turned blue" (2015, interview with Cordy Tymstra, author of The Chinchaga Firestorm, University of Alberta Press, 2014).

scenes.text: September 1950. Across North America and Europe, people saw a blue Sun and Moon.
The smoke came from one fire in Canada, the Chinchaga, burning since June.
On September 24, midday went dark in Ontario. Toronto's streetlights came on by themselves.
People feared a nuclear attack. Historian Cordy Tymstra says the smoke particles were just the right size to turn the Sun blue.
The fire burned up to 17,000 square kilometers, still the largest on record in North America.
